claim: Influenza virus penetrates cells by fusion of viral and endosomal membranes catalyzed by the viral hemagglutinin (HA).
source_text: Influenza virus penetrates cells by fusion of viral and endosomal membranes catalyzed by the viral hemagglutinin (HA).
evidence_reasoning: This is established scientific knowledge about influenza virus entry mechanism.

claim: Withdrawal of the fusion peptide from a pocket in the pre-fusion trimer is rate-limiting for both virion arrest and hemifusion events.
source_text: Effects of mutations in HA indicate that withdrawal of the fusion peptide from a pocket in the pre-fusion trimer is rate-limiting for both events
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is derived from experimental data on HA mutants and their fusion kinetics.

claim: Fusion requires engagement of three or four neighboring HA trimers.
source_text: fusion then requires engagement of three or four neighboring HA trimers
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from analysis of fusion kinetics and computer simulation validation.

claim: A long-lived intermediate state for single, extended HA trimers is a fundamental aspect of the fusion mechanism.
source_text: the requirement for cooperative action of several HAs to bring the fusing membranes together leads to a long-lived intermediate state for single, extended HA trimers. This intermediate is thus a fundamental aspect of the fusion mechanism.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is based on kinetic analysis and the cooperative nature of HA action.

claim: Fusion of two lipid-bilayer membranes is thermodynamically favorable but crosses a high kinetic barrier.
source_text: Fusion of two lipid-bilayer membranes is a thermodynamically favorable process, but it crosses a high kinetic barrier as the two bilayers approach each other.
evidence_reasoning: This is established biophysical knowledge about membrane fusion.

claim: Efficient membrane fusion requires a catalyst, such as a fusion protein or protein complex.
source_text: Efficient fusion therefore requires a catalyst, a role served in living cells by a fusion protein or protein complex.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the requirement for fusion proteins in biological membrane fusion.

claim: The influenza virus hemagglutinin (HA) has become an important paradigm of a fusion catalyst.
source_text: The influenza virus hemagglutinin (HA) has become an important paradigm of a fusion catalyst, in part because of early crystallographic and mechanistic studies and in part because of continued concern about a virus that caused tens of millions of deaths during the 20th century.
evidence_reasoning: This reflects the historical importance of HA in fusion research and the impact of influenza.

claim: HA facilitates fusion by undergoing a large-scale conformational change coupled to the two fusing membranes.
source_text: HA facilitates fusion by undergoing a large-scale conformational change, coupled to the two fusing membranes (virus and target).
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of HA-mediated fusion.

claim: Upon initiating pH exchange, most virions started to move under hydrodynamic force while retaining contacts with the target bilayer.
source_text: Upon initiating the flow of buffer for pH exchange, most virions started to move under the hydrodynamic force while retaining contacts with the target bilayer.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct observation from the single-virion fusion experiments.

claim: Virion arrest at the target membrane is irreversible and invariably precedes hemifusion.
source_text: The particles arrested at various times after the pH drop, but invariably preceding hemifusion (Figure 1B; Video 1). The arrest was irreversible (Videos 2 and 3).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in the experimental videos and data.

claim: Approximately 20% of virions at pH 5.5 and 5.65 had already arrested at the onset of imaging or before the pH drop.
source_text: A subset (approximately 20% at pH 5.5 and 5.65) of virions had already arrested at the onset of imaging or had done so before the pH drop.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative observation from the experiments.

claim: Mean tlag(pHdrop–arrest) is about an order of magnitude shorter than mean tlag(arrest–hemifusion) throughout the tested pH range.
source_text: Mean values for tlag(pHdrop–arrest) and tlag(arrest–hemifusion) show the same pH dependence, with mean tlag(pHdrop–arrest) being about an order of magnitude shorter throughout the tested pH range.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the kinetic analysis.

claim: The distributions for both tlag(pHdrop–arrest) and tlag(arrest–hemifusion) can be fit with a gamma probability density function.
source_text: We can fit the distributions for both
evidence_reasoning: The gamma distribution fitting is a statistical analysis method applied to the experimental data.

claim: Insertion of fusion peptides from 3 or 4 independent HA trimers into the target membrane anchors the particle.
source_text: A simple interpretation of virion arrest is that insertion of fusion peptides from a number of independent HA trimers (3 or 4) into the target membrane anchors the particle.
evidence_reasoning: This interpretation is based on the kinetic data and gamma distribution analysis.

claim: Short incubations of virions with target membranes at pH 5 and 0°C lead to insertion of a small subset of fusion peptides and stable virus anchoring not associated with membrane fusion.
source_text: Bulk experiments have shown that short incubations of virions with target membranes at pH 5 and 0°C lead to insertion of a small subset of fusion peptides and stable virus anchoring not associated with membrane fusion (Tsurudome et al., 1992).
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from previous bulk experiments by Tsurudome et al., 1992.

claim: The HA of Udorn is 97% identical in amino-acid sequence to that of X-31.
source_text: The HA of Udorn is 97% identical in amino-acid sequence to that of X-31
evidence_reasoning: This is a sequence comparison result.

claim: Udorn virions fuse approximately tenfold faster than X31-HA virions at pH 5.5.
source_text: Udorn virions fuse approximately tenfold faster than X31-HA virions at pH 5.5
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative comparison from the experimental measurements.

claim: A substitution of serine for glycine at position four in HA2 might account for the accelerated fusion kinetics of Udorn.
source_text: Comparison of the Udorn and X-31 HA amino-acid sequences suggests that one particular difference might account for the accelerated fusion kinetics of the former—a substitution of serine for glycine at position four in HA2.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from sequence comparison and kinetic differences.

claim: Udorn is the only strain in the database with the S4G substitution in HA2, with glycine being otherwise universally conserved.
source_text: Udorn is the only strain in the database with this substitution, glycine being otherwise universally conserved (Nobusawa et al., 1991; Cross et al., 2009).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on database analysis cited from previous studies.

claim: In the pre-fusion conformation of HA, Gly4HA2 participates in a network of polar hydrogen-bond interactions with the carboxylate of Asp112 HA2.
source_text: In the pre-fusion conformation of HA, Gly4HA2 participates in a network of polar hydrogen-bond interactions with the carboxylate of Asp112 HA2, which is also strictly conserved
evidence_reasoning: This is based on structural studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: A serine substitution at position 4 in HA2 would weaken or interrupt the interaction with Asp112 because glycine has a backbone conformation not allowed for other residues.
source_text: A serine substitution would weaken or interrupt this interaction, because the glycine has a backbone conformation not allowed for other residues.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from structural chemistry principles about glycine's unique conformational properties.

claim: Previous studies have reported an elevated pH threshold of fusion for cell-surface expressed HA harboring substitutions at Gly4 or Asp112.
source_text: Previous studies have reported an elevated pH threshold of fusion for cell-surface expressed HA harboring substitutions at Gly4 or Asp112 (Gething et al., 1986; Steinhauer et al., 1995).
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from previous studies on HA mutants.

claim: D112AHA2 mutations accelerate hemifusion of both Udorn and X31-HA virions at pH 5.5, but the effect on X31-HA is more pronounced.
source_text: D112AHA2 mutations accelerate hemifusion of both Udorn and X31-HA virions, but the effect on the latter is more pronounced (Figure 4A).
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct result from the mutant fusion kinetics experiments.

claim: The G4SHA2 mutation partly destabilizes contacts between the terminal fusion-peptide residues and Asp112HA2.
source_text: We infer from these observations that the G4SHA2 mutation partly destabilizes contacts between the terminal fusion-peptide residues and Asp112HA2
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the kinetic effects of the mutations.

claim: The D112AHA2 change eliminates the source of stability from the Gly4HA2–Asp112HA2 interaction completely.
source_text: the D112AHA2 change then eliminates this source of stability completely
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the complete acceleration of fusion kinetics with this mutation.

claim: None of the mutations change the values of N derived from the pH 5.5 tlag(arrest–hemifusion) distributions.
source_text: None of the mutations change the values of N derived from the pH 5.5 tlag(arrest–hemifusion) distributions (or for static virions, tlag(pHdrop–hemifusion) distributions) (Figure 4B)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from gamma distribution analysis of mutant data.

claim: Release of the fusion peptide from its pre-fusion pocket is a rate-limiting step in the transition from arrest to hemifusion.
source_text: We conclude that for these viruses, release of the fusion peptide from its pre-fusion pocket is a rate-limiting step in the transition from arrest to hemifusion.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is based on the effects of mutations on fusion kinetics.

claim: N is related to the number of HA trimers that must independently expose their fusion peptides before a hemifusion-inducing transition can follow.
source_text: The consistent changes in fusion kinetics produced by the mutations, including the good fit obtained from a probability distribution that assumes concomitant changes in the rates of all N events (see 'Materials and methods'), further support our proposal that N is related to the number of HA trimers that must independently expose their fusion peptides before a hemifusion-inducing transition can follow.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the consistency of the gamma distribution fits across mutants.

claim: The rate of arrest for D112AHA2 variants was too rapid to detect flow-induced motion.
source_text: The rate of arrest for either of the destabilized D112AHA2 variants was too rapid for us to detect flow-induced motion (Videos 7 and 8).
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct observation from the experimental videos.

claim: Fusion-peptide release from its pocket is rate-limiting for virion arrest as well as for hemifusion.
source_text: We therefore could not determine N from arrest distributions for those viruses, but we could nonetheless infer that fusion-peptide release from its pocket is rate-limiting for virion arrest as well as for hemifusion.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the rapid arrest kinetics of the D112A mutants.

claim: At pH 4.5 and below, the mutants have indistinguishable mean values for tlag(pHdrop–hemifusion).
source_text: At pH 4.5 and below, the mutants described above have indistinguishable mean values for tlag(pHdrop–hemifusion) (Figure 4D).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the pH 4.5 experiments.

claim: The lag times become nearly pH independent at pH 4.5 and below, presumably because most of the relevant titrating groups have become protonated.
source_text: Moreover, the lag times have become nearly pH independent, presumably because most of the relevant titrating groups (carboxylates) have become protonated.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the pH-independence of kinetics at low pH.

claim: Fitting the tlag(pHdrop–hemifusion) distributions with a gamma probability density yields unchanged values of N (between 3 and 6) for all the variants at pH 4.5.
source_text: Fitting the tlag(pHdrop–hemifusion) distributions with a gamma probability density yields unchanged values of N (between 3 and 6) for all the variants
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from statistical analysis of the pH 4.5 data.

claim: What changes with pH is not the number of rate-limiting rearrangements leading to hemifusion but only their rate.
source_text: confirming that what changes with pH is not the number of rate-limiting rearrangements leading to hemifusion but only their rate
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is based on the unchanged N values across pH conditions.

claim: Protonation of Asp112 probably explains why mutations that affect stability of the fusion peptide in its pre-fusion pocket have little or no effect on the fusion rate at pH 4.5 and below.
source_text: Protonation of Asp112 probably explains why mutations that affect stability of the fusion peptide in its pre-fusion pocket and influence the fusion rate at pH 5.5 have little or no effect on the fusion rate at pH 4.5 and below.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the pH-dependent effects of the mutations.

claim: Even at pH 4.5, some rate-limiting rearrangement precedes membrane insertion of the fusion peptide.
source_text: The unchanged value of N and the observation that a fraction of the X31-HA WT and S4GHA2Udorn particles show directed motion after the pH drop suggest that even at pH 4.5, some rate-limiting rearrangement precedes membrane insertion of the fusion peptide.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation of directed motion and unchanged N values at pH 4.5.

claim: The steps determining the rate of arrest and the rate of transition from arrest to hemifusion are the same, both limited by the rate of fusion-peptide exposure.
source_text: The influence of mutations at positions 4 and 112 in HA2 on hemifusion at the physiologically relevant pH of 5.5 demonstrates that the steps determining the rate of arrest (from the time of pH drop) and the rate of transition from arrest to hemifusion are the same, that is, both processes are limited by the rate of fusion-peptide exposure.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is based on the similar effects of mutations on both processes.

claim: Both arrest and hemifusion result from the action of several HA trimers each undergoing the rate-limiting rearrangement.
source_text: Both also result from the action of several HA trimers each undergoing this rate-limiting rearrangement as indicated by the unchanged shape of their individual lag time distributions (unchanged value of N) under vastly different proton concentrations
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the unchanged N values across pH conditions.

claim: The rate constants for tlag(pHdrop–arrest) are about five to tenfold greater than those for tlag(arrest-hemifusion).
source_text: The rate constants derived from gamma distribution fitting of the tlag(pHdrop–arrest) data are, however, about five to tenfold greater than those for tlag(arrest-hemifusion)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the gamma distribution analysis.

claim: Virion arrest results from fusion-peptide release and irreversible target-membrane insertion from several HA trimers anywhere in the area of virus-target membrane contact.
source_text: A simple interpretation of these observations is that virion arrest results from fusion-peptide release and irreversible target-membrane insertion from several HA trimers anywhere in the area of virus-target membrane contact
evidence_reasoning: This interpretation is based on the kinetic data and rate constant differences.

claim: Hemifusion requires a specific geometry for the participating HAs, specifically their proximity to each other.
source_text: hemifusion is limited by the same HA rearrangements, fusion-peptide release and membrane insertion, but requires a specific geometry for the participating HAs, that is, their proximity to each other, and is thus related to a different probability
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the different rate constants for arrest and hemifusion despite the same rate-limiting step.

claim: Computer simulation was used to test the predictions of the model and probe the relationship between N and the number of neighboring HA trimers required for hemifusion.
source_text: To test the predictions of our model directly and to probe the relationship between the value of
evidence_reasoning: This describes the computational approach used to validate the experimental model.

claim: Simulation-derived distributions agree remarkably well with experimentally obtained data.
source_text: Simulation-derived distributions agree remarkably well with our experimentally obtained data
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparison between simulation and experimental results.

claim: The simulations predict Na = 3–4 and Nh = 3–4 for a contact patch area of approximately 120 HAs.
source_text: Simulation-derived distributions agree remarkably well with our experimentally obtained data and predict Na = 3–4, Nh = 3–4 and are most consistent with our independently predicted contact patch area of approximately 120 HAs
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the computer simulation analysis.

claim: The gamma-distribution-derived value of N for virion arrest closely approximates the number of trimers leading to arrest, Na.
source_text: The gamma-distribution-derived value of N for virion arrest closely approximates the number of trimers leading to arrest, Na
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from comparing simulation and gamma distribution analysis.

claim: The gamma-distribution-derived value of N for hemifusion is related to the number of neighboring HA trimers participating in hemifusion but only approximates this value for smaller contact patch sizes.
source_text: The gamma-distribution-derived value of N for hemifusion is related to the number of neighboring HA trimers participating in hemifusion, but it only approximates this value for smaller contact patch sizes (close to 50 HA trimers) and is greater than the true Nh for larger patch sizes
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the simulation analysis showing the relationship between apparent and true N values.

claim: The value of Nh = 2 yields a distribution that cannot be approximated by a gamma distribution for any analyzed patch size and value of Na.
source_text: The value of Nh = 2 yields a distribution that cannot be approximated by a gamma distribution for any analyzed patch size and value of Na
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the simulation testing different Nh values.

claim: The experimental data are consistent with Nh = 3–4 for patch sizes between 50 and 150 HA trimers.
source_text: Our experimental data—the gamma-distribution-derived N and the ratio of mean hemifusion and arrest times—are consistent with Nh = 3–4 for patch sizes between 50 and 150 HA trimers.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from comparing experimental and simulation results.

claim: The key parameters (gamma-distribution-derived N value and ratio of mean hemifusion and arrest lag times) are independent of the percentage of active HAs within the contact patch down to a lattice-point occupancy of 40%.
source_text: We found that the key parameters—the gamma-distribution-derived N value and the ratio of mean hemifusion and arrest lag times—are independent of the percentage of active HAs within the contact patch, down to a lattice-point occupancy of 40%
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from simulation testing the effect of inactive HAs.

claim: Reduction in active HA density to 20% yielded a sudden drop in the apparent N derived from gamma-distribution fitting.
source_text: Further reduction in active HA density to 20% yielded a sudden drop in the apparent N derived from gamma-distribution fitting of simulation-derived tlag(arrest–hemifusion) data
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from simulation testing extreme reductions in active HA density.

claim: Many early studies of HA-mediated fusion kinetics relied on fusion of HA-expressing cells with red blood cells or planar bilayers.
source_text: Many early studies of HA-mediated fusion kinetics relied on fusion of HA-expressing cells with red blood cells (Spruce et al., 1989; Zimmerberg et al., 1994) or planar bilayers (Melikyan et al., 1993a, 1993b).
evidence_reasoning: This is a historical summary of previous experimental approaches.

claim: Measurements of conductance and capacitance showed reversible opening and closing of flickering pores following initial acidification.
source_text: In the latter case, measurements of conductance and capacitance showed reversible opening and closing of flickering pores, following initial acidification and commitment to secure pore opening only after a number of seconds.
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from previous planar bilayer fusion studies.

claim: Hill-plot treatment of red-blood cell fusion experiments led to an estimate of 3–4 HAs per fusion event.
source_text: Hill-plot treatment of the fusion times led to an estimate of 3–4 HAs per fusion event.
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from previous cell-cell fusion experiments by Danieli et al., 1996.

claim: Single-virion fusion experiments confirmed the earlier estimate of 3–4 HAs and showed that lipid-mixing precedes content mixing.
source_text: Single-virion fusion experiments confirmed the earlier estimate of 3–4 HAs and showed that lipid-mixing precedes content mixing, as expected for an obligatory hemifusion intermediate (Floyd et al., 2008).
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from previous single-virion experiments by Floyd et al., 2008.

claim: The pathway with the lowest energy barrier for hemifusion appears to be through a 'hemifusion stalk' derived from the apposed leaflets.
source_text: The pathway with the lowest energy barrier appears to be through a so-called 'hemifusion stalk', derived from the apposed leaflets (Kuzmin et al., 2001).
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from continuum model calculations by Kuzmin et al., 2001.

claim: Some proposals suggest that a stalk can expand into a 'hemifusion diaphragm' or open directly into a pore.
source_text: Some proposals for the subsequent transition to a fusion pore postulate expansion of the stalk into a 'hemifusion diaphragm', in which the distal leaflets form a continuous bilayer between the two membrane-bounded compartments; others suggest that a stalk can open directly into a pore.
evidence_reasoning: This summarizes different theoretical proposals for fusion pore formation.

claim: Hemifusion diaphragms can be seen by electron microscopy.
source_text: Hemifusion diaphragms can be seen by electron microscopy (e.g., Hernandez et al., 2012)
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from electron microscopy studies.

claim: Evidence for stalk-like structures comes from x-ray analysis of crystalline lipid phases.
source_text: evidence for stalk-like structures comes from x-ray analysis of crystalline lipid phases (Yang and Huang, 2002)
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from x-ray crystallography studies.

claim: Calculations and observations suggest that hemifusion diaphragms are stable, long-lived intermediates and that their formation might be a dead-end side reaction.
source_text: Both calculations and observations suggest that hemifusion diaphragms are stable, long-lived intermediates and that their formation might be a dead-end side reaction.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from various theoretical and experimental studies.

claim: SNARE/synaptotagmin/complexin-mediated fusion of lipid vesicles proceeds too quickly (<100 ms) to detect even a hemifusion intermediate.
source_text: Recent work on calcium-triggered SNARE/synaptotagmin/complexin-mediated fusion of lipid vesicles on a physiological time scale shows that the reaction proceeds too quickly (<100 ms) to detect even a hemifusion intermediate
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from recent SNARE fusion studies by Diao et al., 2012.

claim: Fusion from a hemifusion diaphragm is slow (tens of seconds) and inefficient in SNARE-mediated fusion.
source_text: fusion from a hemifusion diaphragm is slow (tens of seconds) and inefficient (Diao et al., 2012)
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from SNARE fusion studies by Diao et al., 2012.

claim: Tight packing of proteins on the viral surface probably makes a transition from stalk to diaphragm even less likely in influenza-virus fusion than in SNARE-mediated fusion.
source_text: In influenza-virus fusion, tight packing of proteins on the viral surface probably makes a transition from stalk or other point-contact intermediate to diaphragm even less likely than in SNARE-mediated fusion, in which protein coverage of the fusing membranes is sparser.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from comparing protein density on viral and SNARE-mediated fusion systems.

claim: The experiments provide strong evidence for a long-lived, extended HA intermediate.
source_text: They provide strong evidence for a long-lived, extended HA intermediate and for a rapid and cooperative transition to lipid mixing when a critical number of these intermediates has accumulated within a contact neighborhood.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from the kinetic experiments and mutant analysis.

claim: There is a rapid and cooperative transition to lipid mixing when a critical number of extended intermediates has accumulated within a contact neighborhood.
source_text: for a rapid and cooperative transition to lipid mixing when a critical number of these intermediates has accumulated within a contact neighborhood
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the kinetic data and simulation results.

claim: Binding to sialic-acid-containing glycans is weak, and local forces can displace the particle.
source_text: Binding to sialic-acid-containing glycans is weak, and local forces, such as flow, can displace the particle
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the observed particle motion and known properties of HA-sialic acid interactions.

claim: The contact region between a virus particle and the target membrane is relatively large, probably 50–150 HA trimers.
source_text: The contact region between a virus particle and the target membrane is relatively large (probably 50–150 HA trimers, depending on the particle morphology
evidence_reasoning: This is estimated from particle dimensions and HA spacing.

claim: The probability of arrest is the probability for fusion-peptide exposure and insertion from 3–4 trimers within the area of membrane contact.
source_text: the probability of arrest is then the probability for fusion-peptide exposure and insertion from 3–4 trimers within the area of membrane contact
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the kinetic analysis and simulation results.

claim: HA trimers independently undergo the first part of their low-pH-induced conformational change and pause as extended intermediates with their fusion peptides inserted into the target membrane.
source_text: The data suggest that HA trimers independently undergo the first part of their low-pH-induced conformational change and pause as extended intermediates with their fusion peptides inserted into the target membrane.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the kinetic data showing different rates for arrest and hemifusion.

claim: Capture by the target membrane restrains a trimer from collapsing to induce hemifusion until 2–3 neighbors help generate sufficient pull to deform the membrane.
source_text: Capture by the target membrane restrains a trimer from collapsing to induce hemifusion until 2–3 neighbors help generate sufficient pull to deform the membrane.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the requirement for neighboring HAs and the kinetic data.

claim: When the conditions for hemifusion have been met, the final HA rearrangements are fast and cooperative.
source_text: This interpretation also argues that when these conditions have been met, the final HA rearrangements are fast and cooperative.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the kinetic data and the sensitivity to mutations.

claim: Cooperativity of the final HA conformational rearrangements can derive either from contacts between neighboring HAs or from linkage by virtue of their common insertion in the two hemifusing membranes.
source_text: Cooperativity of the final HA conformational rearrangements can derive either from contacts between neighboring HAs or simply from the linkage that is present among all participating HAs by virtue of their common insertion in the two hemifusing membranes.
evidence_reasoning: This presents two possible mechanisms for cooperativity.

claim: The authors favor the explanation that cooperativity derives from linkage through common membrane insertion rather than direct HA-HA contacts.
source_text: We favor the latter explanation.
evidence_reasoning: This is the authors' interpretation based on the lack of evidence for lateral HA contacts.

claim: There is no evidence for defined, lateral contacts between HA trimers.
source_text: There is no evidence for defined, lateral contacts between HA trimers
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the lack of structural evidence for such contacts.

claim: Any lateral contacts between HAs could not persist during the substantial changes in HA conformation and orientation that accompany the progression to hemifusion.
source_text: any such contacts, were they present, could not persist during the substantial changes in HA conformation and orientation that accompany the progression to hemifusion
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the large conformational changes known to occur in HA.

claim: Evidence for the rapidity of the final HA rearrangements comes from the results of simulation and gamma distribution analysis and the sensitivity of the derived rate constant to mutations.
source_text: Evidence for the rapidity of the final HA rearrangements comes from the results of our simulation and gamma distribution analysis and the sensitivity of the derived rate constant to the mutations we have introduced.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the computational and experimental analysis.

claim: Any additional steps not directly sensitive to the mutations must be faster than any one of the steps of fusion-peptide engagement with the target membrane.
source_text: Any additional steps, not directly sensitive to those mutations, must be faster than any one of the steps of fusion-peptide engagement with the target membrane.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the rate-limiting nature of fusion-peptide release.

claim: Engagement of the fusion peptide with a target membrane requires formation of an extended intermediate to project it beyond the outer margin of adjacent HA1 heads.
source_text: Engagement of the fusion peptide with a target membrane requires formation of an extended intermediate to project it beyond the outer margin of adjacent HA1 heads
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the structural constraints of the HA trimer.

claim: For an extended intermediate to form, the HA1 heads must dissociate from their contact with an HA2 loop between residues 58–74.
source_text: For an intermediate to form that resembles the inner core of the ultimate, low-pH triggered structure (as drawn for the extended structure in Figure 1A), the HA1 heads must dissociate from their contact with an HA2 loop (HA2 residues 58–74: see Figure 3D) between the short first α-helix (HA2, residues 38–57) and the long central α-helix (HA2, residues 75–127)
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from structural analysis of pre- and post-fusion HA conformations.

claim: Extension of the central trimeric coiled-coil probably drives the reversal and helical conversion of the HA2 loop.
source_text: Extension of the central trimeric coiled-coil probably drives the latter process, as the amino-acid sequence of the loop strongly favors such a conformation
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from sequence analysis and cited structural studies.

claim: The extended intermediate would project the fusion peptide no more than about 25 Å beyond the palisade of un-triggered HAs.
source_text: The structure thus pictured would project the fusion peptide no more than about 25 Å beyond the palisade of un-triggered HAs
evidence_reasoning: This is estimated from structural modeling of the extended intermediate.

claim: The intermediate that mediates arrest and hemifusion must be almost completely extended, at least for part of its lifetime.
source_text: In short, the intermediate that mediates arrest and hemifusion must indeed be almost completely extended, at least for part of its lifetime.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the structural constraints and the need to project the fusion peptide.

claim: Breaking the interactions that restrain the fusion peptide is rate-limiting both for virion arrest and for hemifusion at the pH of endosomes (approximately 5 to 5.5).
source_text: Our results show that breaking the interactions that restrain the fusion peptide is rate-limiting both for virion arrest and for hemifusion at the pH of endosomes from which influenza virus penetrates (approximately 5 to 5.5)
evidence_reasoning: This is concluded from the mutational analysis and kinetic data.

claim: This interpretation is consistent with the dominance hierarchy of mutations that influence the threshold pH for fusion.
source_text: this interpretation is consistent with the dominance hierarchy of mutations that influence the threshold pH for fusion (Steinhauer et al., 1996)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cited previous studies on pH threshold mutations.

claim: Mutations that affect the pH dependence of fusion map to a number of sites distributed across the HA2 trimer interface.
source_text: Mutations that affect the pH dependence of fusion map to a number of sites distributed across the HA2 trimer interface (Daniels et al., 1985).
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from previous mutational studies.

claim: Changes in the stability of the HA2 trimer interface will influence fluctuations from the equilibrium structure and hence the 'window of opportunity' for the fusion peptide to withdraw productively from its pocket.
source_text: Changes in the stability of this interface will influence fluctuations from the equilibrium structure and hence the 'window of opportunity' for the fusion peptide to withdraw productively from its pocket.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the relationship between structural stability and conformational dynamics.

claim: The fusion-peptide contacts are conserved in all field-isolated influenza HA virions and form upon cleavage of HA0.
source_text: The fusion-peptide contacts, conserved in all field-isolated influenza HA virions, form upon cleavage of HA0 (Chen et al., 1998; Russell et al., 2004).
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from structural studies on HA maturation.

claim: The stability of fusion-peptide contacts is critical for viral transmission during passage from one host to another and during entry.
source_text: Their stability is critical for viral transmission, not only in the passage from one host or cell to another, but also during entry
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the functional importance of controlled fusion timing.

claim: Fusion will be relatively unproductive if it occurs before the pH has dropped enough to allow M2-mediated acidification of the particle interior.
source_text: as fusion will be relatively unproductive if it occurs before the pH of the surrounding compartment has dropped enough to allow M2-mediated acidification of the particle interior (Ivanovic et al., 2012)
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the requirement for RNP release and cited from previous studies.

claim: M2-mediated acidification of the particle interior induces dissociation of the eight ribonucleoproteins (RNPs) of the viral genome from the matrix protein, M1.
source_text: which induces dissociation of the eight ribonucleoproteins (RNPs) of the viral genome from the matrix protein, M1 (Martin and Helenius, 1991)
